title: Messenger database operations
description: Fixed application SQL operations, transaction phases, connection pools and numeric PostgreSQL diagnosis. Application timings and server digest statistics have different boundaries. No raw SQL is exported.

panels.title: Operations ranked by accumulated query time
panels.description: Top 15 fixed operations by accumulated application query lifecycle seconds in the selected range. Concurrent work can exceed elapsed wall time. Mean, calls and failures use the selected range. p95 and p99 use the rate interval at its end. These are application measurements and cannot be joined to PostgreSQL query IDs.

panels.title: Query lifecycle mean and p95
panels.description: Lifecycle includes jOOQ rendering, connection acquisition when needed, preparation, binding, JDBC execution, eager fetching and resource closing. A lazy query completes at cursor close. Idle operations have no percentile.

panels.title: Query lifecycle p99
panels.description: Histogram estimates across selected service replicas. Compare calls and failures before interpreting a tail, especially at low volume.

panels.title: Query lifecycle calls per second
panels.description: One lifecycle observation per jOOQ execution. A batch lifecycle can contain several statement execution phases.

panels.title: Query lifecycle failure ratio
panels.description: Failed lifecycle observations divided by all lifecycle observations. Zero appears only for operations with observed calls. A failed SQL call does not establish the final transaction outcome.

targets.expr: (sum by (operation) (rate(messenger_database_query_seconds_count{job=~"$service",operation=~"$operation",outcome="failure"}[$__rate_interval])) or on(operation) (0 * sum by (operation) (rate(messenger_database_query_seconds_count{job=~"$service",operation=~"$operation"}[$__rate_interval])))) / sum by (operation) (rate(messenger_database_query_seconds_count{job=~"$service",operation=~"$operation"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Statement execution mean and p95
panels.description: Each jOOQ executeStart through executeEnd phase includes JDBC driver and network work. Result fetching can do further I/O after this phase. Batch phases can repeat within one query lifecycle.

panels.title: Result fetching mean and p95
panels.description: jOOQ fetchStart through fetchEnd phases, recorded only when a fetch phase exists. Fetching can include driver and network I/O. This overlaps the full query lifecycle; do not add percentiles.

panels.title: Transaction mean and p95
panels.description: Actual new Spring transactions from beforeBegin through completion listener callback. Includes begin and transaction work, plus completion synchronizations observed by the listener. Excludes later connection cleanup. Joined transactions do not add another transaction. Query Operation filter does not apply here.

panels.title: Transaction outcomes per second
panels.description: Completion classifications are committed, rolled_back, failed and begin_failed. Rollback can be intentional. Failed completion may have an uncertain durable outcome. This timer does not replace SQL request deduplication.

panels.title: Transaction phase mean
panels.description: Begin includes connection acquisition and transaction setup. Active includes application work and precompletion synchronizations. Commit includes observed commit/completion callbacks and postcommit synchronizations. Rollback follows its listener callbacks. These boundaries are not direct JDBC commit or WAL fsync timers.

panels.title: Transaction phase p95
panels.description: Separate histograms per operation and phase. Do not add phase, query or transaction percentiles. Failure samples remain included in each phase distribution.

panels.title: Connection acquisition p95 and p99
panels.description: Hikari time waiting for a pooled connection, by service replica and pool. Empty buckets have no percentile.

panels.title: Pool utilization
panels.description: Active connections divided by configured pool maximum per replica. Publishers hold one active connection for LISTEN. This baseline is not evidence of transaction load.

panels.title: Waiting borrowers and acquisition timeouts
panels.description: Pending borrowers are instantaneous. Timeout counters increase when acquisition times out. Counts and events per second use separate axes.

panels.title: Connection usage p95
panels.description: Time from checkout until return to Hikari, sampled on return. The publisher LISTEN connection can contribute a long usage sample at shutdown. Usage is not transaction duration.

panels.title: Backend states by role
panels.description: PostgreSQL activity snapshots by fixed JDBC ApplicationName. Unattributed and non-application connections may also appear. Five-second scraping misses short waits.

panels.title: Active backend wait events
panels.description: Active client backends with a nonempty wait category. A wait category describes the sampled instant and cannot measure accumulated wait duration.

panels.title: Current blocked and waiting backends
panels.description: Numeric aggregate counts for messenger client backends, excluding the exporter connection. Lock waiters currently wait for a PostgreSQL lock. I/O and client waits include active backends only.

panels.title: Oldest query and transaction ages
panels.description: Lock query age starts at query_start, so it includes work before waiting and is not exact lock-wait time. Idle transaction age starts at xact_start. Zero means no matching sampled backend.

panels.title: WAL synchronization mean
panels.description: Global WAL synchronization time divided by synchronizations. Includes all database work. No synchronization in the interval means no mean. This is not a per-send commit timer.

panels.title: Database deadlocks per second
panels.description: PostgreSQL database deadlock counter. Other locking stalls may occur without a deadlock.

panels.title: Exported digests ranked by execution time
panels.description: Top 15 within the exporter subset, selected by interval execution seconds. Exporter v0.20.1 exports at most 25 entries ordered by cumulative server execution time and excludes its lowest-time percentile. Missing entries and churn can undercount the selected interval. Query IDs have no verified mapping to fixed application operations.

panels.title: Exported digest mean execution time
panels.description: Rate of server execution seconds divided by calls for the continuously observed exported subset. pg_stat_statements has no latency histogram and cannot provide p95 or p99.

panels.title: Exported digest calls per second
panels.description: Calls within the exported subset. Top-N selection is cumulative and is not a complete interval ranking across all database statements.

panels.title: Digest readiness and collector health
panels.description: Each readiness value should be 1. Custom query errors and cumulative application recording failures should be 0. Missing metrics indicate unavailable telemetry. The one-shot extension installation must finish before exporter startup.

panels.title: Digest entries and retained query ID series
panels.description: Current call-series count is at most 25 per exporter scrape. Distinct query IDs seen in the selected range can exceed 25. pg_stat_statements.max bounds server entries, not Prometheus series over seven days.

targets.legendFormat: Query ID series in selected range

panels.title: Digest entry deallocations per second
panels.description: An increase means PostgreSQL evicted least-used statement entries. Rates and totals for replaced entries can be incomplete.

panels.title: Digest statistics age and reset changes
panels.description: Age since the global statistics reset. Targeted pg_stat_statements_reset calls may reset individual entries without changing the global timestamp. Counter decreases and exporter churn also limit interval accounting.
